query: Reported superconducting high-entropy alloys are dominated by Nb-Ta matrices, while other studies concern titanium-rich systems based on heavy transition metals and partly ordered systems. Consequently, these precedents do not establish what controls superconductivity in high-entropy alloys outside the best-studied material classes. Within the defining constraint of a solid solution containing at least five elements at no less than 5 atomic percent each, what governs superconducting behavior in such an uncharacterized high-entropy alloy, and why? State one testable mechanistic hypothesis, a controlled comparison against the starting material, predicted observations relative to the baseline, applicable boundary conditions, the earlier evidence supporting the hypothesis, and an outcome that would falsify it.

generation.hypothesis: Local lattice distortions arising from the atomic size mismatch among the constituent elements modulate the electron–phonon coupling strength, thereby governing superconductivity (Tc and critical fields) in uncharacterized high-entropy alloys.
generation.material_initial_state: A high-entropy alloy solid solution composed of at least five elements (each at ≥5 at.%) with significant atomic size variation—such as a Ti-rich or NbTi-based system combined with heavy transition metals.
generation.intervention: Substitute one or more larger or smaller atoms with an element of similar electronic character but closer in atomic radius to reduce the degree of lattice distortion, while keeping the overall valence electron count and chemical composition similar.
generation.conditions: Synthesize both the baseline alloy and the modified alloy under identical processing conditions, ensuring a homogeneous single-phase BCC solid solution, and carry out superconducting measurements at cryogenic temperatures.
generation.structural_mediator: Local lattice distortions induced by atomic size mismatch.
generation.mechanism: The atomic size mismatch leads to local lattice distortions that alter the bond lengths and modify the local electronic density of states at the Fermi level, thereby enhancing the electron–phonon coupling. Reducing these distortions should weaken the coupling effect, leading to changes in the superconducting transition temperature (Tc) and the upper critical field.
generation.predicted_outcome: The modified alloy with reduced atomic size mismatch (and hence reduced local lattice distortions) is predicted to show a lower Tc and a decreased upper critical field compared to the baseline alloy.
generation.baseline: The original high-entropy alloy, such as Nb0.34Ti0.33Zr0.14Ta0.11Hf0.08, which exhibits significant atomic size variations and superconducting properties (e.g., Tc ~7.5 K and high critical field).
generation.boundary: This hypothesis is applicable within the regime of HEAs where the electronic structures of the substituted elements remain similar and the only significant change is in the magnitude of local lattice distortions. If compositional changes introduce other effects (e.g., significant changes in carrier density or introduce additional scattering centers), the mechanism may not hold.
generation.uncertainty: Direct quantitative correlations between measured local lattice distortions and electron–phonon coupling strength in these alloys are not yet well established, so while lattice distortion is a plausible mediator, other disorder effects or electronic structure nuances may also play influential roles.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two series of HEA samples: one with the baseline composition (e.g., Nb0.34Ti0.33Zr0.14Ta0.11Hf0.08) and one with modified composition where one or more elements are replaced by those with closer atomic radii (but similar valence electrons) to reduce lattice distortions. Characterize both series structurally (using XRD and EXAFS) and electronically (via measurements of Tc and upper critical field).
measurements: X-ray diffraction for lattice parameter consistency and estimation of disorder
EXAFS to quantify local bonding distortions and atomic environments
Magnetization and resistivity measurements to determine Tc
Critical field measurements to determine Hc2
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If reducing the atomic size mismatch (and hence lattice distortions) does not result in a measurable decrease in electron–phonon coupling indicators (e.g., lower Tc or reduced Hc2) or if superconducting properties remain unchanged despite the reduction in local distortions, then the hypothesis that local lattice distortions govern superconductivity in these HEAs would be falsified.

## Abstract
The structural and physical properties of the new titanium- and niobium-rich type-A high-entropy alloy (HEA) superconductor Nb0.34Ti0.33Zr0.14Ta0.11Hf0.08 (in at.%) were studied by X-ray powder diffraction, energy dispersive X-ray spectroscopy, magnetization, electrical resistivity, and specific heat measurements. In addition, electronic structure calculations were performed using two complementary methods: the Korringa–Kohn–Rostoker Coherent Potential Approximation (KKR-CPA) and the Projector Augmented Wave (PAW) within Density Functional Theory (DFT). The results obtained indicate that the alloy exhibits type II superconductivity with a critical temperature close to 7.5 K, an intermediate electron–phonon coupling, and an upper critical field of 12.2(1) T. This finding indicates that Nb0.34Ti0.33Zr0.14Ta0.11Hf0.08 has one of the highest upper critical fields among all known HEA superconductors.

## Abstract
AbstractHigh-entropy alloys (HEA) form through the random arrangement of five or more chemical elements on a crystalline lattice. Despite the significant amount of resulting compositional disorder, a subset of HEAs enters a superconducting state below critical temperatures, Tc<10 K. The superconducting properties of the known HEAs seem to suffice a Bardeen–Cooper–Schrieffer (BCS) description, but little is known about their superconducting order parameter and the microscopic role of disorder. We report on magnetic susceptibility measurements on films of the superconducting HEA (TaNb)1-x(ZrHfTi)x for characterizing the lower and upper critical fields Hc,1(T) and Hc,2(T), respectively as a function of temperature T. Our resulting analysis of the Ginzburg–Landau coherence length and penetration depth demonstrates that HEAs of this type are single-band isotropic s-wave superconductors in the dirty limit.
